_comment: The catalogue. Pure data — no code reads anything here it cannot also read
from a file you edit by hand.
ROUGHNESS IS THE ART DIRECTION. Centuries-old architecture is almost
entirely diffuse: stone that was ever polished has been walked and weathered
matte, old oak absorbs light rather than returning it, wool and leather have
no specular lobe worth the name. Values here sit deliberately high — 0.9+ on
everything structural — and the only surfaces allowed a visible highlight are
burnished brass edges, crystal, lenses and fresh wax. If a surface in this
building is catching the light, that should be a decision someone made.
Scan sources live in sources.json; `npm run textures:fetch` pulls them.

wood_walnut_ancient.label: Ancient dark walnut
wood_walnut_ancient.note: The keeper's own furniture. Near-black in the recesses, warm where a thousand years of hands have polished it.

wood_oak_carved.label: Hand-carved oak
wood_oak_carved.note: Chisel facets, not machine edges. Dust sits in every cut.

wood_mahogany_weathered.label: Weathered mahogany
wood_mahogany_weathered.note: Varnish gone uneven and crazed. Water marks near the floor.

wood_shelving_library.label: Old library shelving
wood_shelving_library.note: Darker oil stain along every shelf edge where books have been pulled out for centuries.

wood_floor_polished.label: Polished hardwood flooring
wood_floor_polished.note: Running-bond planks. Walked bare along the desire lines, dull and dusty under the shelves.

wood_panel_carved.label: Decorative carved panels
wood_panel_carved.note: Wainscot with sunk fields. Relief belongs in the normal map, never in geometry.

wood_rotunda_wainscot.label: Rotunda wainscot
wood_rotunda_wainscot.note: The drum's panelling. Warmer and lighter than the halls' — the rotunda is the room that has been kept up, and the timber shows it.

wood_rotunda_timber.label: Rotunda timber
wood_rotunda_timber.note: Beams and framing under the dome.

wood_hall_wainscot.label: Hall wainscot
wood_hall_wainscot.note: Deliberately a SEPARATE definition from the rotunda's, not a shared one. The halls are meant to read as their own timber — a visitor notices the change walking out of the drum, and that change is the only thing distinguishing eight long corridors from the room they lead off. Tones currently match; the point is that they can diverge without touching a line of geometry code.

wood_hall_timber.label: Hall timber
wood_hall_timber.note: The darker oak of the wings' beams and ceilings — the wood that makes the halls read as a different room from the rotunda.

wood_gallery_timber.label: Gallery timber
wood_gallery_timber.note: The upper gallery's framing — between the rotunda's tone and the halls'.

stone_dome_coffer.label: Dome coffering
stone_dome_coffer.note: The great dome's inner shell. Deep stepped coffers with lapis fields and gilt celestial engraving, weathered from the oculus down. `color` is WHITE on purpose: the painter already bakes the stone's own tone into the map, so tinting it a second time here multiplies the albedo by itself and the whole shell goes to near-black. Any painter that takes a base colour has this hazard.

stone_vault_coffer.label: Vault coffering
stone_vault_coffer.note: The wings' barrel soffits — a gilt star at the centre of every coffer. WHITE colour on purpose: the painter is handed the tone, and setting it here as well multiplied it in twice, which for a dark teal is very near black — only the rib and the gilt star survived it and the soffit read as a grid on nothing. Same fix stone_dome_coffer had. The tone lives in the painter's args below.

wood_table_top.label: Reading table top
wood_table_top.note: Lighter and more polished than the shelving — a working surface, rubbed bright at the elbows, ink-stained at the edges.

wood_bark_old.label: Old oak limb
wood_bark_old.note: For the timber order in the halls, and for the roots that have got in.

stone_limestone_ancient.label: Ancient limestone
stone_limestone_ancient.note: The building's own body. Micro-cracks, chipped arrises, a millennium of dust in the mouldings.

stone_granite_dark.label: Dark granite
stone_granite_dark.note: Plinths, thresholds, the bases that take the wear.

stone_sandstone_weathered.label: Weathered sandstone
stone_sandstone_weathered.note: Eroded soft. Water staining runs downward wherever the roof has ever failed.

stone_marble_white.label: White marble
stone_marble_white.note: The statues. Veined, slightly translucent at the edges, grey in every crevice.

stone_flagstone_floor.label: Flagstone flooring
stone_flagstone_floor.note: Uneven slabs, polished hollow along the walking lines, lichen only where damp collects.

stone_pillar_carved.label: Carved pillar stone
stone_pillar_carved.note: Fluted shafts and their capitals. Corners knocked off at shoulder height.

stone_hearth.label: Hearth stone
stone_hearth.note: Rough coursed blocks around the fire. Soot-blackened above the opening — the only surface in the building with real smoke damage.

stone_dressed_plain.label: Dressed stone, plain face
stone_dressed_plain.note: Benches, case plinths, sills — worked stone with no coursing or fluting on it. Its stand-in is a flat field on purpose: a block or flute pattern painted onto a bench seat reads as wallpaper.

stone_arcade_ashlar.label: Arcade ashlar
stone_arcade_ashlar.note: The halls' recessed fields. Damp, cold, greener than the rotunda's stone — the arcade is the part of the building the weather has got into.

stone_arcade_flutes.label: Arcade fluted shaft
stone_arcade_flutes.note: Cut from the same damp base stone as the bays. Its own definition rather than a tint of the pillar stone, because the flute canvas bakes its base in — tinting on top turned the shafts nearly black against near-white capitals.

stone_arcade_upper.label: Arcade upper stage
stone_arcade_upper.note: Drier and warmer than the base — the stage above the damp line.

stone_arcade_base.label: Arcade base stone
stone_arcade_base.note: Plain worked faces of the halls' stone order — members in front of the ashlar fields, so no coursing painted on them.

wood_arcade_timber.label: Arcade oak members
wood_arcade_timber.note: The bark-clad oak rolls of the halls' order. The canvas bakes its own base, so this is used untinted.

stone_plaster_vault.label: Vault plaster
stone_plaster_vault.note: Candle soot gathers on the ribs and in the coffer heads.

stone_niche_mosaic.label: Niche conch mosaic
stone_niche_mosaic.note: The gold-tessera semi-dome over each statue. Gold over crimson is the historic apse pairing — same warmth, different value — and it is what makes the vault and the damask below read as one surface rather than two materials meeting at a line. Brick was tried here and fought the hanging. Set straight on the map and fanned into a radial vault by the quarter-sphere's own UVs, the way a mosaicist sets an apse.

metal_bronze_aged.label: Aged bronze
metal_bronze_aged.note: Cast and hammered. Oxidised to a dark olive in the recesses, rubbed back to warm metal on every raised edge. Hammer facets, not a smooth surface.

metal_brass_burnished.label: Burnished brass
metal_brass_burnished.note: Lantern bodies, orrery arms, drawer pulls. Aged lacquer over the metal, gone amber and crazed; bright only along the arrises fingers actually reach. Never a mirror — a clean specular on brass is the fastest way to make a hand-forged building look machined.

metal_copper_oxidized.label: Oxidized copper
metal_copper_oxidized.note: Verdigris creeping out of the joints and running down.

metal_iron_forged.label: Forged iron
metal_iron_forged.note: Drawn under a hammer and black-oxidised. Scale, pitting, and the faint flat facets a smith leaves. Almost no specular — this is the metal that disappears.

metal_gold_leaf.label: Gold leaf
metal_gold_leaf.note: Gilding on the dome's constellations and the coffer rosettes. Worn through to bole in places.

book_cloth_oxblood.label: Cloth binding, oxblood
book_cloth_oxblood.note: The same bookbinding linen as book_cloth_binding in its other published colourway — two cloth grounds so a shelf is not one bolt of fabric.

book_spine_gilt.label: Gilt-embossed spine atlas
book_spine_gilt.note: An atlas, not a tile — every shelf reads a different cell so no two spines repeat.

fabric_rug_persian.label: Persian rug
fabric_rug_persian.note: Faded to a third of its dyed strength. Frayed at the ends, worn to the warp where feet cross it.

fabric_cosmographia_mandala.label: Cosmographia — the rotunda mandala
fabric_cosmographia_mandala.note: The observatory floor: one 31 m sheet, never tiled. Woven orbit rings, a twelvefold zodiac band, a stone pavement course and the ambulatory the ten ways leave from. Walked to the warp along every gate line.

fabric_ceremonial_way.label: Cosmographia — the ceremonial way
fabric_ceremonial_way.note: The radial carpet out of the mandala and down every hall. u runs across the way, v along it, so only v repeats; the selvedges are frayed into the alpha so the boards show past them.

stone_observatory_roundel.label: Cosmographia — the observatory roundel
stone_observatory_roundel.note: The compass-rose disc set into the boards where a way pauses at a gallery. Cut edge, not a selvedge — this one is masonry.

fabric_velvet_banner.label: Velvet banner
fabric_velvet_banner.note: Sheen is the whole point — velvet reads as velvet only when the grazing angle lights up.

leather_upholstery.label: Chair leather
leather_upholstery.note: The keeper's fireside chairs. The stand-in is painted neutral so the tint carries the colour — swap in a scan and drop the tint.

fabric_niche_damask.label: Statue niche damask
fabric_niche_damask.note: The crimson field behind every niched figure — the deep red the great museum rotondas hang their marbles against, and what sets a pale statue off the dark timber drum. Its own definition rather than a tint of the wool hanging, because it has to survive the lighting rig: at 85% shadow a plain #6d222a alcove goes to brown mud and the red disappears. Lifted about a stop, plus a very dark emissive that raises the floor of the colour without flattening it — the baked vertex shading still multiplies the diffuse, so the hollow keeps its depth.

glass_crown_old.label: Old crown glass
glass_crown_old.note: Wavy, bubbled, never optically flat. Distortion is what makes a window read as a thousand years old.

decal_star_chart.label: Celestial chart
decal_star_chart.note: Projected, never modelled. Alpha-cut so it sits on whatever surface it is pinned to.

misc_fern.label: Fern
misc_fern.note: A shuttlecock of pinnate fronds, drawn springing from the bottom centre so a cross-quad carrying it stands in a pot rather than floating. alphaTest, never transparent.

misc_palm.label: Parlour palm
misc_palm.note: Long strap leaves bowing over under their own weight — the tall pots. Fewer, bigger shapes than the fern, because these are read against a wall from below.

misc_shrub.label: Flowering shrub
misc_shrub.note: A dense dome of small leaves with five-petalled blossoms scattered through it.

misc_trail.label: Trailing creeper
misc_trail.note: Drawn head-DOWN: runners spring from the top of the sheet and fall, accelerating as they go. Serves both the pot skirts and the long creepers off the rotunda gallery.

misc_soil.label: Potting earth
misc_soil.note: Dark crumb, grit, fallen leaf and a little moss — the surface of a pot that has been watered for a very long time.

stone_terracotta.label: Terracotta
stone_terracotta.note: The pots. Wheel-thrown, salt-bloomed, chipped at the rim and a good deal duller than a garden-centre pot — these have stood indoors for centuries.

metal_bronze_frieze.label: Bronze astronomical frieze
metal_bronze_frieze.note: The cast band under the gallery cornice: zodiac wreaths and instruments in low relief, verdigris in the hollows, the proud parts rubbed back to metal. The relief is PAINTED — this surface must never take an albedo scan, only normal/roughness. Metalness is kept low and a touch of emissive added: there is no environment map in this scene, so a physically-metal band fourteen metres up in an 85%-shadow room renders as a black stripe.

stone_celestial_roundel.label: Celestial roundels (atlas)
stone_celestial_roundel.note: Eight carved medallions in one atlas so the ten round the drum cost one draw call. UVs are addressed per cell — never give this a repeat other than 1.

stone_constellation_plaque.label: Constellation plaques (atlas)
stone_constellation_plaque.note: The ten small cut plaques set over the statues, one per pier, in a single atlas. Cut in stone rather than brass on purpose: a bright plate here would outshine the figure standing under it.
